answer: Each of 277 aliases needs its own gig histories, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. A ceilidh band membership with gig booking history works as the gate: gigs played under one band name across seasons. The jetty check is what stops the copy-paste farm: The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The prism record is public, the ocean cost is per identity, and 277 aliases cost 277 times one honest seat.
